name: Global Cypher Query Contract
description: Mandatory rules the Cypher agent must apply to EVERY generated query against the Worktual OKG. Retrieve and prepend this card on every request.
business_rules: CASE SENSITIVITY: Neo4j labels, relationship types and property names are case-sensitive. Labels are PascalCase (Conversation, SalesOrder, ContactProfile). Relationship types are UPPER_SNAKE_CASE (HAS_ROUTING_ATTEMPT, BELONGS_TO_SEGMENT). Properties are lower_snake_case (created_at, churn_score, total_amount). Never title-case a property, never PascalCase a relationship, never UPPER a label.

NODE KEYS ARE NOT ALWAYS 'id'. Registry: Contact=cdp_id, CustomerScore=cdp_id, ContactPoint=identity_id, Insight=insight_id, Recommendation=recommendation_id, Segment=segment_id, Order=order_id, OrgProfile=organization_id, KnowledgeOrgProfile=organization_id, AssignmentSettings=organization_id, WebchatChannelConfig=channel_config_id, SocialChannelConfig=channel_config_id, Product=id (bigint), PlatformProduct=id (string). Every other label uses id.

ANCHOR BOTH ENDS WITH LABELS. These relationship types are overloaded and reused across unrelated pairs: CONTAINS, HAS_LINE, FOR_PRODUCT, FOR_CONTACT, FOR_DEAL, FOR_ACTIVITY, FOR_COMPANY, OWNED_BY, CREATED_BY, ASSIGNED_TO, IN_QUEUE, FROM_QUEUE, HANDLED_BY, OFFERED_AGENT, FOLLOWS_HOURS, USES_TEMPLATE, APPROVED_BY. Never write (a)-[:CONTAINS]->(b) without labels on both a and b.

TENANT SCOPE IS THE DATABASE. Each tenant has its own Neo4j database. Do NOT add `WHERE n.organization_id = $organization_id` unless the runtime actually binds $organization_id — an unbound parameter makes Neo4j throw 'Expected parameter(s)' and the agent returns an error instead of an answer.

DATETIME vs DATE. Most timestamps are ZONED DATETIME (UTC) and must be compared with datetime($period_start). But DATE-typed columns must be compared with date($period_start): Invoice.issue_date, Deal.expected_close_date, Contact.acquisition_date, Contact.date_of_birth, Holiday.holiday_date, Quote.valid_until. Mixing date and datetime raises a type error.

DURATIONS. Use duration.inSeconds(a, b).seconds for elapsed time. duration.between(a, b).seconds returns ONLY the seconds component (excludes days/months) and silently under-reports any span longer than 24 hours.
ALWAYS BOUND BOTH ENDS OF A PERIOD: `>= datetime($period_start) AND < datetime($period_end)`. A start-only filter makes 'this week' silently mean 'this week and everything after'.
GUARD DIVISION: CASE WHEN total = 0 THEN 0.0 ELSE toFloat(numerator)/total END. A bare toFloat(x)/0 returns null and the answer reads as 'unknown'.
EXISTENCE CHECKS: use EXISTS { (c)-[:HAS_TRANSFER]->(:Transfer) } or COUNT {}. Bare pattern expressions outside WHERE are removed in Neo4j 5.

NEVER INVENT A TENANT FAN-OUT EDGE. The following (Tenant)-[...]->(x) relationships are commented out in core.yaml and DO NOT EXIST in the graph: HAS_CONTACT, HAS_CONTACT_PROFILE, HAS_CONVERSATION, HAS_INTERACTION, HAS_DEAL, HAS_DEAL_ACTIVITY, HAS_COMPANY, HAS_COMPANY_SITE, HAS_QUOTE, HAS_PROPOSAL, HAS_INVOICE, HAS_SALES_ORDER, HAS_CONTRACT, HAS_NOTIFICATION, HAS_MISSED_CONTACT, HAS_SHARED_NOTE, HAS_KNOWLEDGE_DOCUMENT, HAS_QUOTE_TEMPLATE, HAS_PROPOSAL_TEMPLATE, HAS_INVOICE_TEMPLATE. Match the label directly instead: MATCH (d:Deal) — not MATCH (:Tenant)-[:HAS_DEAL]->(d:Deal), which returns zero rows.

(Contact)-[:PARTICIPATED_IN]->(Conversation) DOES NOT EXIST. Conversations, interactions, activities, insights and recommendations hang off a Contact through synthetic collection nodes. See concept_contact_history.
IF NO CARD MATCHES, SAY SO. Do not improvise labels or relationship types that are absent from these cards.
search_text: global query contract case sensitivity node keys tenant scope datetime duration overloaded relationships

name: Contact History Traversal (collection nodes)
description: A Contact does not connect directly to its Conversations, Interactions, Activities, Insights or Recommendations. Each hangs off a synthetic collection node keyed by the same cdp_id. Every 'show me everything about customer X' query must go through the collection hop.
disambiguation: This is the ONLY correct path from a person to their history. (Contact)-[:PARTICIPATED_IN]->(Conversation), (Contact)-[:HAS_CONVERSATION]->(Conversation) and (Tenant)-[:HAS_CONVERSATION]->() are all non-existent and return zero rows.
business_rules: (Contact)-[:HAS_CONVERSATIONS]->(ConversationHistory)-[:CONTAINS]->(Conversation)
(Contact)-[:HAS_INTERACTIONS]->(InteractionHistory)-[:CONTAINS]->(Interaction)
(Contact)-[:HAS_ACTIVITIES]->(ActivityTimeline)-[:CONTAINS]->(ContactActivity)
(Contact)-[:HAS_INSIGHTS]->(InsightCollection)-[:CONTAINS]->(Insight)
(Contact)-[:HAS_RECOMMENDATIONS]->(RecommendationCollection)-[:CONTAINS]->(Recommendation)
Note the plural relationship names: HAS_CONVERSATIONS / HAS_INTERACTIONS / HAS_ACTIVITIES / HAS_INSIGHTS / HAS_RECOMMENDATIONS. Singular forms do not exist.
All five collection nodes are keyed by cdp_id, the same value as the Contact.
CONTAINS is overloaded — it is also (Order)-[:CONTAINS]->(Product). Always label both ends.

Direct edges that DO exist from other nodes to Contact: (ContactProfile)-[:OVERLAY_OF]->(Contact), (Contact)-[:HAS_SCORES]->(CustomerScore), (Contact)-[:HAS_CONTACT_POINT]->(ContactPoint) — direction is Contact→ContactPoint, (Contact)-[:HAS_CHANNEL_IDENTITY]->(ChannelIdentity), (Contact)-[:PLACED]->(Order), (Contact)-[:BELONGS_TO_SEGMENT]->(Segment), (Contact)-[:HAS_ENRICHMENT]->(LeadEnrichmentSnapshot), (Contact)-[:HAS_LEAD_SUMMARY]->(LeadSummary).
cypher_template: MATCH (ct:Contact {cdp_id: $cdp_id})-[:HAS_CONVERSATIONS]->(:ConversationHistory)-[:CONTAINS]->(c:Conversation) RETURN c.id AS conversation_id, c.channel AS channel, c.status AS status, c.created_at AS created_at, c.resolved_at AS resolved_at ORDER BY c.created_at DESC LIMIT 20
examples: Show me all conversations for this customer
What insights do we have on contact X?
Give me the activity timeline for this lead
search_text: contact history collection nodes HAS_CONVERSATIONS HAS_INTERACTIONS HAS_ACTIVITIES HAS_INSIGHTS HAS_RECOMMENDATIONS CONTAINS customer 360 timeline

name: Missed Contacts
description: A contact that was offered to a specific agent and not answered. Materialised as its own MissedContact node with reason, channel, offered_at and missed_at.
disambiguation: Three different things are often called 'missed'. (1) Agent was offered and did not answer -> MissedContact node (THIS card). (2) Routing could not find any agent to offer to -> RoutingAttempt.outcome, see concept_routing_failure. (3) Customer hung up before any agent -> see concept_abandonment_rate. Do not answer a MissedContact question with RoutingAttempt data or the numbers will not reconcile with the Missed Contacts screen in the product.
business_rules: MissedContact is a first-class node (ccass.agent_missed_contacts). Key = id. Do not derive it from RoutingAttempt.
Use missed_at for the event date. offered_at is when the offer went out, acknowledged_at is when the agent cleared it.
Available relationships: (MissedContact)-[:MISSED_BY]->(Agent), -[:ASSIGNED_USER]->(User), -[:FROM_CONVERSATION]->(Conversation), -[:FROM_QUEUE]->(Queue), -[:FOR_CONTACT]->(Contact).
There is NO (Tenant)-[:HAS_MISSED_CONTACT]->(MissedContact) edge — match (mc:MissedContact) directly.
Grouping dimensions available directly on the node without a join: channel, reason, customer_name, customer_email, customer_phone.
The Agent-side name is Agent.display_name, not Agent.name.
For 'why did it increase', run the diagnostic_template ONCE — it returns dimension, current, previous, delta in a single pass.
cypher_template: MATCH (mc:MissedContact) WHERE mc.missed_at >= datetime($period_start) AND mc.missed_at < datetime($period_end) RETURN count(mc) AS missed_count
diagnostic_template: MATCH (mc:MissedContact)-[:FROM_QUEUE]->(q:Queue) WITH q.name AS dimension, sum(CASE WHEN mc.missed_at >= datetime($period_start) AND mc.missed_at < datetime($period_end) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS current, sum(CASE WHEN mc.missed_at >= datetime($compare_start) AND mc.missed_at < datetime($compare_end) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS previous WHERE current > 0 OR previous > 0 RETURN dimension, current, previous, current - previous AS delta ORDER BY abs(current - previous) DESC LIMIT 5
examples: Why did missed contacts increase this week?
Which queue has the most missed contacts?
Which agent missed the most contacts?
search_text: missed contacts MissedContact missed_at MISSED_BY FROM_QUEUE agent did not answer week over week

name: Routing Failure / No Agent Available
description: Attempts by the router to place a conversation with an agent, and their outcomes. Used for capacity and coverage questions, not for agent-level missed contacts.
disambiguation: This is the routing engine's view. For an agent who was offered and did not answer use concept_missed_contacts. For a customer who left the queue use concept_abandonment_rate.
business_rules: (Conversation)-[:HAS_ROUTING_ATTEMPT]->(RoutingAttempt) — direction is Conversation to RoutingAttempt.
(RoutingAttempt)-[:TARGETED_QUEUE]->(Queue) and (RoutingAttempt)-[:OFFERED_AGENT]->(Agent).

OUTCOME VALUES ARE NOT GUARANTEED. Never hard-code an outcome list. Run the discovery query first: MATCH (ra:RoutingAttempt) RETURN DISTINCT ra.outcome AS outcome, count(*) AS n ORDER BY n DESC. Filtering on a value that does not exist returns 0 and reads as 'no problems this week', which is the worst possible wrong answer.
Use ra.created_at for when the attempt was made and ra.completed_at for when it resolved.
attempt_number lets you separate first offers from retries; count DISTINCT conversations, not attempts, when the question is about contacts rather than offers.
cypher_template: MATCH (ra:RoutingAttempt) WHERE ra.created_at >= datetime($period_start) AND ra.created_at < datetime($period_end) RETURN ra.outcome AS outcome, count(ra) AS attempts, count(DISTINCT ra.conversation_id) AS conversations ORDER BY attempts DESC
diagnostic_template: MATCH (ra:RoutingAttempt)-[:TARGETED_QUEUE]->(q:Queue) WITH q.name AS dimension, sum(CASE WHEN ra.created_at >= datetime($period_start) AND ra.created_at < datetime($period_end) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS current, sum(CASE WHEN ra.created_at >= datetime($compare_start) AND ra.created_at < datetime($compare_end) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS previous WHERE current > 0 OR previous > 0 RETURN dimension, current, previous, current - previous AS delta ORDER BY abs(current - previous) DESC LIMIT 5
discovery_template: MATCH (ra:RoutingAttempt) RETURN DISTINCT ra.outcome AS outcome, count(*) AS n ORDER BY n DESC
examples: How often did routing fail to find an agent?
Which queue has the worst coverage?
search_text: routing failure RoutingAttempt outcome HAS_ROUTING_ATTEMPT TARGETED_QUEUE no ready agents coverage

name: Abandonment Rate
description: Share of conversations where the customer disconnected before any agent was assigned.
disambiguation: Customer-side. For agent-side non-answer use concept_missed_contacts; for router-side failure use concept_routing_failure.
business_rules: Abandoned = ended_at IS NOT NULL AND assigned_at IS NULL.
end_reason and end_actor carry the reason; end_actor distinguishes customer-initiated from system-initiated. Discover the values before filtering on them rather than assuming codes.
Denominator is all conversations created in the period. Guard against a zero denominator.
Conversation has NO queue_id property in the graph — group by queue only through (Conversation)-[:IN_QUEUE]->(Queue). Group by channel using the scalar c.channel property, which is always populated.
cypher_template: MATCH (c:Conversation) WHERE c.created_at >= datetime($period_start) AND c.created_at < datetime($period_end) WITH count(c) AS total, sum(CASE WHEN c.assigned_at IS NULL AND c.ended_at IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS abandoned RETURN abandoned, total, CASE WHEN total = 0 THEN 0.0 ELSE round(100.0 * abandoned / total, 2) END AS abandonment_pct
diagnostic_template: MATCH (c:Conversation) WHERE c.created_at >= datetime($compare_start) AND c.created_at < datetime($period_end) WITH c.channel AS dimension, sum(CASE WHEN c.created_at >= datetime($period_start) AND c.assigned_at IS NULL AND c.ended_at IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS current, sum(CASE WHEN c.created_at < datetime($compare_end) AND c.assigned_at IS NULL AND c.ended_at IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS previous RETURN dimension, current, previous, current - previous AS delta ORDER BY abs(current - previous) DESC LIMIT 5
examples: What is our abandonment rate this week?
Which channel has the highest abandonment?
search_text: abandonment rate customer disconnect hung up before agent assigned_at null ended_at

name: SLA Breach Rate
description: Conversations whose service level deadline was missed, recorded as SLAInstance.breached_at.
business_rules: (Conversation)-[:HAS_SLA]->(SLAInstance)-[:BASED_ON]->(SLA). TRACKED_BY_SLA and HAS_SLA_INSTANCE do not exist.
The instance label is SLAInstance (from ccass.conversation_sla_state); the policy label is SLA (from ccass.sla_policies). Both are uppercase SLA — not Sla, not SlaInstance.

Breached when SLAInstance.breached_at IS NOT NULL. Filter breached_at within the period for 'breaches this week'; filter Conversation.created_at within the period for 'breach rate of this week's conversations'. These are different questions — pick deliberately and say which you used.
Conversation also carries denormalised sla_status, first_response_due_at and resolution_due_at. Prefer SLAInstance for breach facts; Conversation.sla_status is a snapshot and can lag.
SLA policy name lives on SLA.name; warning thresholds on SLA.warning_threshold_pct.
cypher_template: MATCH (c:Conversation)-[:HAS_SLA]->(si:SLAInstance) WHERE si.breached_at >= datetime($period_start) AND si.breached_at < datetime($period_end) RETURN count(si) AS breach_count
diagnostic_template: MATCH (c:Conversation)-[:HAS_SLA]->(si:SLAInstance)-[:BASED_ON]->(s:SLA) WITH s.name AS dimension, sum(CASE WHEN si.breached_at >= datetime($period_start) AND si.breached_at < datetime($period_end) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS current, sum(CASE WHEN si.breached_at >= datetime($compare_start) AND si.breached_at < datetime($compare_end) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS previous WHERE current > 0 OR previous > 0 RETURN dimension, current, previous, current - previous AS delta ORDER BY abs(current - previous) DESC LIMIT 5
examples: How many SLA breaches this month?
Which SLA policy has the most breaches?
search_text: SLA breach SLAInstance breached_at HAS_SLA BASED_ON policy overdue response resolution

name: First Contact Resolution (FCR)
description: Conversations resolved without any transfer to another queue or agent.
business_rules: FCR = resolved_at IS NOT NULL AND no (Conversation)-[:HAS_TRANSFER]->(:Transfer).
Use EXISTS { } for the negation. Bare pattern expressions inside CASE are invalid in Neo4j 5.
Report the rate, not just the count — a raw fcr_count with no denominator is meaningless.

A conversation with CONTINUES_FROM set is a follow-up of a previous contact and arguably not FCR. If the question is about true first-time resolution, exclude them: NOT EXISTS { (c)-[:CONTINUES_FROM]->(:Conversation) }.
cypher_template: MATCH (c:Conversation) WHERE c.resolved_at >= datetime($period_start) AND c.resolved_at < datetime($period_end) WITH count(c) AS resolved, sum(CASE WHEN NOT EXISTS { (c)-[:HAS_TRANSFER]->(:Transfer) } THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS fcr RETURN fcr, resolved, CASE WHEN resolved = 0 THEN 0.0 ELSE round(100.0 * fcr / resolved, 2) END AS fcr_pct
search_text: first contact resolution FCR HAS_TRANSFER resolved_at no transfer rate

name: Average Handle Time (AHT)
description: Average elapsed seconds from agent assignment to resolution.
business_rules: AHT = duration.inSeconds(c.assigned_at, c.resolved_at).seconds. Do NOT use duration.between(...).seconds — it drops the day component and under-reports any conversation open longer than 24 hours, which is common on email.
Only include rows where both assigned_at and resolved_at are non-null.
Anchor the period on resolved_at (when the handling finished), and bound both ends.
Always return the sample size alongside the average — a 3-conversation average should not be reported as a trend.
Per-agent breakdown goes through (Conversation)-[:HANDLED_BY]->(Agent), returning Agent.display_name.
Email conversations skew AHT heavily. Split by c.channel before comparing periods.
cypher_template: MATCH (c:Conversation) WHERE c.resolved_at >= datetime($period_start) AND c.resolved_at < datetime($period_end) AND c.assigned_at IS NOT NULL RETURN round(avg(duration.inSeconds(c.assigned_at, c.resolved_at).seconds)) AS aht_seconds, count(c) AS sample_size
diagnostic_template: MATCH (c:Conversation) WHERE c.assigned_at IS NOT NULL AND c.resolved_at >= datetime($compare_start) AND c.resolved_at < datetime($period_end) WITH c.channel AS dimension, avg(CASE WHEN c.resolved_at >= datetime($period_start) THEN duration.inSeconds(c.assigned_at, c.resolved_at).seconds END) AS current, avg(CASE WHEN c.resolved_at < datetime($compare_end) THEN duration.inSeconds(c.assigned_at, c.resolved_at).seconds END) AS previous RETURN dimension, round(current) AS current, round(previous) AS previous, round(coalesce(current,0) - coalesce(previous,0)) AS delta ORDER BY abs(coalesce(current,0) - coalesce(previous,0)) DESC LIMIT 5
search_text: average handle time AHT assigned_at resolved_at duration inSeconds HANDLED_BY

name: Service Level
description: Share of conversations whose first agent response landed inside the first-response SLA deadline.
disambiguation: Service Level measures responses that were on time. SLA Breach Rate measures the ones that were not. They should sum to 100% over the same population — if they do not, you have filtered on different anchors.
business_rules: Met when c.first_agent_response_at <= si.first_response_due_at.
Use first_agent_response_at, NOT first_response_at — first_response_at includes bot responses and will inflate service level on any channel where bot_active is true.
Guard the denominator.
Conversations with no first_agent_response_at are unanswered so far; decide explicitly whether they count as a miss (they usually should for a closed period) and state the choice.
cypher_template: MATCH (c:Conversation)-[:HAS_SLA]->(si:SLAInstance) WHERE c.created_at >= datetime($period_start) AND c.created_at < datetime($period_end) WITH count(c) AS total, sum(CASE WHEN c.first_agent_response_at IS NOT NULL AND c.first_agent_response_at <= si.first_response_due_at THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS met RETURN met, total, CASE WHEN total = 0 THEN 0.0 ELSE round(100.0 * met / total, 2) END AS service_level_pct
search_text: service level first_agent_response_at first_response_due_at answered within threshold percentage

name: Queue Wait Time
description: Elapsed seconds from entering the queue to agent assignment.
business_rules: Wait = duration.inSeconds(c.queued_at, c.assigned_at).seconds. Never duration.between(...).seconds.
Conversation has no queue_id property — the queue name is only reachable via (Conversation)-[:IN_QUEUE]->(Queue), returning q.name.

Conversations still waiting (assigned_at IS NULL) are excluded by this metric and will make wait time look better than it is during a backlog. Report the count of still-waiting conversations alongside.
Bound both ends of the period on created_at.
cypher_template: MATCH (c:Conversation)-[:IN_QUEUE]->(q:Queue) WHERE c.created_at >= datetime($period_start) AND c.created_at < datetime($period_end) AND c.queued_at IS NOT NULL AND c.assigned_at IS NOT NULL RETURN q.name AS queue, round(avg(duration.inSeconds(c.queued_at, c.assigned_at).seconds)) AS avg_wait_seconds, count(c) AS sample_size ORDER BY avg_wait_seconds DESC LIMIT 10
examples: Which queue has the longest wait?
search_text: queue wait time queued_at assigned_at IN_QUEUE speed of answer average

name: Transfer Rate
description: Conversations transferred to another queue or agent, as a count and as a share of conversations in the period.
business_rules: (Conversation)-[:HAS_TRANSFER]->(Transfer). Destination queue via (Transfer)-[:TRANSFERRED_TO]->(Queue); origin queue via (Transfer)-[:FROM_QUEUE]->(Queue).
Agent-side edges are FROM_AGENT, REQUESTED_AGENT and OFFERED_AGENT — all to Agent.
A conversation can have several Transfer nodes. Count DISTINCT conversations for a rate, count Transfer nodes for transfer volume, and say which you did.
Transfer.state tells you whether the transfer completed. requested_at is the anchor date; completed_at may be null for abandoned transfers.
Transfers are the inverse population of FCR — reconcile the two when both appear in one answer.
cypher_template: MATCH (c:Conversation)-[:HAS_TRANSFER]->(t:Transfer) WHERE t.requested_at >= datetime($period_start) AND t.requested_at < datetime($period_end) RETURN count(DISTINCT c) AS conversations_transferred, count(t) AS transfer_events
diagnostic_template: MATCH (c:Conversation)-[:HAS_TRANSFER]->(t:Transfer)-[:TRANSFERRED_TO]->(q:Queue) WITH q.name AS dimension, sum(CASE WHEN t.requested_at >= datetime($period_start) AND t.requested_at < datetime($period_end) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS current, sum(CASE WHEN t.requested_at >= datetime($compare_start) AND t.requested_at < datetime($compare_end) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS previous WHERE current > 0 OR previous > 0 RETURN dimension, current, previous, current - previous AS delta ORDER BY abs(current - previous) DESC LIMIT 5
examples: Which queue receives the most transfers?
search_text: transfer rate HAS_TRANSFER TRANSFERRED_TO FROM_QUEUE escalation handoff

name: Conversation Volume
description: Count of conversations in a period, optionally split by channel, queue or status.
business_rules: Default to the scalar c.channel property for channel splits. It is always populated. The (Conversation)-[:THROUGH]->(Channel) edge depends on channel_config_id, which is null for a meaningful share of rows — grouping through it silently drops those conversations and undercounts total volume.

If the question needs the configured channel name rather than the channel kind, use (Conversation)-[:THROUGH]->(ch:Channel) and return ch.name, but state that rows without a channel config are excluded.
Channel node properties are channel_type and name. Conversation.channel is the kind (voice, email, webchat, whatsapp...).
Do not mix Conversation counts with Interaction counts in one total — Interaction is a CDP projection of the same event. See concept_interaction.
cypher_template: MATCH (c:Conversation) WHERE c.created_at >= datetime($period_start) AND c.created_at < datetime($period_end) RETURN c.channel AS channel, count(c) AS volume ORDER BY volume DESC
diagnostic_template: MATCH (c:Conversation) WITH c.channel AS dimension, sum(CASE WHEN c.created_at >= datetime($period_start) AND c.created_at < datetime($period_end) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS current, sum(CASE WHEN c.created_at >= datetime($compare_start) AND c.created_at < datetime($compare_end) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS previous WHERE current > 0 OR previous > 0 RETURN dimension, current, previous, current - previous AS delta ORDER BY abs(current - previous) DESC LIMIT 5
search_text: conversation volume count channel queue created_at THROUGH

name: Interaction (CDP projection)
description: Interaction is the CDP-side projection of a CCaaS Conversation, carrying sentiment, outcome and summary for customer-360 use.
disambiguation: Interaction and Conversation describe the SAME event. Never count both in one metric and never join them into one row set — you will double count. Use Conversation for operational contact-centre metrics (SLA, AHT, queue, routing). Use Interaction for customer-level analytics (sentiment, outcome, engagement history).
business_rules: (Interaction)-[:PROJECTED_FROM]->(Conversation) links the two.
(Contact)-[:HAS_INTERACTIONS]->(InteractionHistory)-[:CONTAINS]->(Interaction) is the only path from a person.
Interaction also has (Interaction)-[:IN_QUEUE]->(Queue) and (Interaction)-[:HANDLED_BY]->(Agent) — the same relationship types Conversation uses. Always label the source node or you will match both.
Sentiment, outcome and summary live only on Interaction, not on Conversation.
cypher_template: MATCH (i:Interaction) WHERE i.started_at >= datetime($period_start) AND i.started_at < datetime($period_end) RETURN i.sentiment AS sentiment, count(i) AS interactions ORDER BY interactions DESC
examples: What is the sentiment split of interactions this month?
search_text: interaction CDP projection PROJECTED_FROM sentiment outcome summary InteractionHistory

name: Support Agent
description: The Agent node is the contact-centre identity of a workforce User. Conversations attach to it via HANDLED_BY.
business_rules: (Agent)-[:IS_AGENT_FOR]->(User) — the Agent is the child; the User is the workforce record.
(Agent)-[:HAS_SKILL]->(Skill), (Queue)-[:HAS_MEMBER]->(Agent), (Queue)-[:REQUIRES_SKILL]->(Skill).
(Conversation)-[:HANDLED_BY]->(Agent). Never ASSIGNED_TO for a conversation-to-agent link.
ASSIGNED_TO exists but points to a User, from two different sources: (ContactProfile)-[:ASSIGNED_TO]->(User) and (ContactActivity)-[:ASSIGNED_TO]->(User). Label both ends.
(Conversation)-[:ASSIGNED_USER]->(User) also exists in parallel with HANDLED_BY. Use HANDLED_BY for agent productivity; ASSIGNED_USER only when the question is explicitly about the platform user.
Display name is Agent.display_name. User has first_name and last_name separately — there is no User.name or User.full_name.
(Agent)-[:HAS_PRESENCE]->(AgentPresence) is directed FROM Agent. Same for HAS_CAPACITY to AgentCapacity.
(Tenant)-[:HAS_AGENT]->(Agent) DOES exist (unlike most Tenant fan-outs), but matching (a:Agent) directly is cheaper.
cypher_template: MATCH (c:Conversation)-[:HANDLED_BY]->(a:Agent) WHERE c.created_at >= datetime($period_start) AND c.created_at < datetime($period_end) RETURN a.display_name AS agent, count(c) AS handled ORDER BY handled DESC LIMIT 10
examples: Which agents handled the most conversations?
Which agents are available right now?
search_text: support agent IS_AGENT_FOR HANDLED_BY HAS_SKILL HAS_MEMBER presence capacity display_name

name: Customer
description: A Contact who has bought. Available two ways: the :Customer sublabel set from contact_type, or a completed Order / SalesOrder.
disambiguation: Two definitions coexist and give different numbers. (1) Declared: Contact carries the extra label :Customer because contact_type = 'customer'. (2) Behavioural: the Contact has a completed order. State which you used. If the user asks 'how many customers', prefer the declared sublabel; if they ask 'how many customers bought', use orders.
business_rules: Contact key is cdp_id, NOT id. MATCH (ct:Contact {cdp_id: $cdp_id}).
Sublabels are applied in addition to Contact: :Lead, :Prospect, :Customer, from contact_type. MATCH (ct:Contact:Customer) is the fast path and uses the label index.
CDP purchase path: (Contact)-[:PLACED]->(Order). CRM purchase path: (SalesOrder)-[:PLACED_BY]->(Contact) — note the reversed direction.

Order (cdp.orders, key order_id, amount field total_amount) and SalesOrder (crm.sales_orders, key id, amount field total) are DIFFERENT nodes for different flows. Do not sum them together without knowing the tenant runs only one.

Order status values are not fixed by the schema. Pass them as a parameter ($paid_statuses) rather than hard-coding ['completed','paid'], and run a discovery query if unsure: MATCH (o:Order) RETURN DISTINCT o.status, count(*).
total_amount and total are decimal-mapped. If the CDC consumer wrote them as strings, sum() fails — coerce with toFloat() when in doubt.
cypher_template: MATCH (ct:Contact:Customer) RETURN count(ct) AS customer_count
alternate_template: MATCH (ct:Contact)-[:PLACED]->(o:Order) WHERE o.status IN $paid_statuses RETURN count(DISTINCT ct) AS purchasing_customers
discovery_template: MATCH (o:Order) RETURN DISTINCT o.status AS status, count(*) AS n ORDER BY n DESC
examples: How many customers do we have?
search_text: customer Contact cdp_id Customer sublabel PLACED Order PLACED_BY SalesOrder buyer

name: Lead
description: A Contact in the pre-sale stage. Expressed two ways: the :Lead sublabel from contact_type, and the CRM overlay ContactProfile.lead_status.
disambiguation: Do not confuse the CDP sublabel with the CRM overlay. Contact:Lead is what the CDP thinks the person is. ContactProfile.lead_status is what the sales team set. They disagree regularly. Also distinguish Lead (a person) from Deal (an opportunity) — a converted lead is still a Contact, with (ContactProfile)-[:CONVERTED_TO]->(Deal).
business_rules: (ContactProfile)-[:OVERLAY_OF]->(Contact) — the overlay points AT the Contact. ContactProfile.account_contact_id equals Contact.cdp_id.
Unconverted lead: cp.lead_status IS NOT NULL AND NOT EXISTS { (cp)-[:CONVERTED_TO]->(:Deal) }.
(Contact)-[:HAS_LEAD_SUMMARY]->(LeadSummary) and (Contact)-[:HAS_ENRICHMENT]->(LeadEnrichmentSnapshot) hang off the Contact, NOT off the ContactProfile. Do not route these through ContactProfile.
Ownership: (ContactProfile)-[:ASSIGNED_TO]->(User) for the rep, (ContactProfile)-[:CREATED_BY]->(User) for the creator.
Employment: (ContactProfile)-[:WORKS_AT]->(Company), (ContactProfile)-[:AT_SITE]->(CompanySite). Both are null for B2C tenants.
Qualification fields live on ContactProfile: bant_budget, bant_authority, bant_need, bant_timeline, lead_source, lead_status, disqualify_reason, nurture_status.
There is no (Tenant)-[:HAS_CONTACT_PROFILE]->() edge — match (cp:ContactProfile) directly.
cypher_template: MATCH (cp:ContactProfile)-[:OVERLAY_OF]->(ct:Contact) WHERE cp.lead_status IS NOT NULL AND NOT EXISTS { (cp)-[:CONVERTED_TO]->(:Deal) } RETURN count(DISTINCT ct) AS open_lead_count
diagnostic_template: MATCH (cp:ContactProfile) WHERE cp.lead_source IS NOT NULL WITH cp.lead_source AS dimension, sum(CASE WHEN cp.created_at >= datetime($period_start) AND cp.created_at < datetime($period_end) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS current, sum(CASE WHEN cp.created_at >= datetime($compare_start) AND cp.created_at < datetime($compare_end) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS previous WHERE current > 0 OR previous > 0 RETURN dimension, current, previous, current - previous AS delta ORDER BY abs(current - previous) DESC LIMIT 5
search_text: lead ContactProfile OVERLAY_OF lead_status lead_source CONVERTED_TO Deal LeadSummary enrichment BANT

name: Churn Risk
description: Contacts with an elevated churn_score on their CustomerScore node.
business_rules: (Contact)-[:HAS_SCORES]->(CustomerScore) — plural SCORES. HAS_SCORE does not exist.
CustomerScore key is cdp_id, the same value as the Contact — there is one score node per contact, not one per model run.
Available scores: engagement_score, value_score, loyalty_score, churn_score, purchase_probability, retention_score, advocacy_score, web_engagement_score, intent_score, digital_activity_score.

Score scale is not declared in the schema. Do not assume 0-1 versus 0-100. Sanity-check with: MATCH (cs:CustomerScore) RETURN min(cs.churn_score), max(cs.churn_score), avg(cs.churn_score). A threshold of 0.7 against a 0-100 scale returns everybody.
Always return updated_at with the score so the answer can flag stale scoring.
Contact name is first_name + last_name; there is no Contact.name.
cypher_template: MATCH (ct:Contact)-[:HAS_SCORES]->(cs:CustomerScore) WHERE cs.churn_score >= $threshold RETURN ct.cdp_id AS cdp_id, ct.first_name AS first_name, ct.last_name AS last_name, cs.churn_score AS churn_score, cs.updated_at AS scored_at ORDER BY cs.churn_score DESC LIMIT 20
discovery_template: MATCH (cs:CustomerScore) RETURN min(cs.churn_score) AS min_score, max(cs.churn_score) AS max_score, avg(cs.churn_score) AS avg_score, count(cs) AS scored_contacts
examples: Which customers are at high churn risk?
search_text: churn risk CustomerScore HAS_SCORES churn_score retention_score threshold at risk

name: Customer Lifetime Value (CLV)
description: Total order value attributable to a contact.
business_rules: CDP: (Contact)-[:PLACED]->(Order), sum o.total_amount. CRM: (SalesOrder)-[:PLACED_BY]->(Contact), sum so.total.
DO NOT sum both paths in one query unless you have confirmed the tenant uses both without overlap — for B2B2C tenants the same purchase can appear in each and CLV will double.
Filter to realised revenue by status; do not include cancelled or draft orders in a lifetime value figure.
Multi-currency: Order carries a currency property. Summing across currencies is meaningless — group by currency or filter to one.
CustomerScore.value_score is a model output, not money. Never present it as CLV.
cypher_template: MATCH (ct:Contact)-[:PLACED]->(o:Order) WHERE o.status IN $paid_statuses RETURN ct.cdp_id AS cdp_id, ct.first_name AS first_name, ct.last_name AS last_name, o.currency AS currency, sum(toFloat(o.total_amount)) AS clv, count(o) AS orders ORDER BY clv DESC LIMIT 20
search_text: customer lifetime value CLV LTV Order total_amount PLACED SalesOrder total currency

name: Segment Membership
description: Contacts belonging to a marketing or analytics segment.
business_rules: (Contact)-[:BELONGS_TO_SEGMENT]->(Segment). IN_SEGMENT and MEMBER_OF_SEGMENT do not exist. MEMBER_OF exists but is (User)-[:MEMBER_OF]->(Team) — a different thing entirely.
Segment key is segment_id, not id. Display name is segment_name, not name.
(Tenant)-[:DEFINES_SEGMENT]->(Segment) does exist and is safe to use.
A Contact can be in many segments — count DISTINCT contacts when totalling across segments.
cypher_template: MATCH (ct:Contact)-[:BELONGS_TO_SEGMENT]->(s:Segment) RETURN s.segment_name AS segment, count(DISTINCT ct) AS members ORDER BY members DESC
examples: How many contacts in the VIP segment?
search_text: segment membership BELONGS_TO_SEGMENT segment_name segment_id DEFINES_SEGMENT audience

name: AI Insights and Recommendations
description: Model-generated insights and recommendations attached to a contact through collection nodes.
business_rules: (Contact)-[:HAS_INSIGHTS]->(InsightCollection)-[:CONTAINS]->(Insight). The collection hop is mandatory — Contact does not connect to Insight directly.
(Contact)-[:HAS_RECOMMENDATIONS]->(RecommendationCollection)-[:CONTAINS]->(Recommendation).
Insight key is insight_id; Recommendation key is recommendation_id. Neither uses id.
The collection nodes are keyed by cdp_id, so you can also enter from the collection side: MATCH (ic:InsightCollection {cdp_id: $cdp_id})-[:CONTAINS]->(i:Insight).
Insight fields: insight_type, score, summary, explanation, generated_at. Recommendation fields: recommendation_type, recommendation, confidence, generated_at.
CONTAINS is overloaded — always label the collection node and the child node.
cypher_template: MATCH (ct:Contact {cdp_id: $cdp_id})-[:HAS_INSIGHTS]->(:InsightCollection)-[:CONTAINS]->(i:Insight) RETURN i.insight_type AS type, i.score AS score, i.summary AS summary, i.generated_at AS generated_at ORDER BY i.generated_at DESC LIMIT 10
examples: What insights do we have for this customer?
search_text: AI insight recommendation HAS_INSIGHTS HAS_RECOMMENDATIONS InsightCollection CONTAINS next best action

retrieval.name: Deal Pipeline
retrieval.not_this: Lead = a person (ContactProfile). Deal = an opportunity.

contract.template: MATCH (d:Deal) WHERE d.closed_at IS NULL RETURN d.stage AS stage, count(d) AS deals, sum(toFloat(d.amount)) AS pipeline_value ORDER BY pipeline_value DESC
contract.discover: MATCH (d:Deal) RETURN DISTINCT d.stage AS stage, count(*) AS n ORDER BY n DESC

name: Account (Company)
description: Account is not a label. The organisational entity is Company, with CompanySite for individual locations.
disambiguation: Do not confuse Company (a customer organisation) with Tenant (the Worktual customer who owns the database). Tenant comes from accounts.organizations; Company comes from crm.companies. A question about 'our company' means Tenant; a question about 'accounts' or 'clients' means Company.
business_rules: MATCH (co:Company) DIRECTLY. (Tenant)-[:HAS_COMPANY]->(Company) is commented out in core.yaml and returns zero rows.
(Company)-[:HAS_SITE]->(CompanySite) — direction is Company to site. (Company)-[:PARENT_COMPANY]->(Company) for hierarchy; traverse it with *0.. carefully, it can be deep.
(ContactProfile)-[:WORKS_AT]->(Company) links people. Contact itself does NOT link to Company — you must go through the ContactProfile overlay.
(Deal)-[:WITH_COMPANY]->(Company), (Contract)-[:FOR_COMPANY]->(Company), (SalesOrder)-[:FOR_COMPANY]->(Company), (Invoice)-[:ISSUED_TO]->(Company). Note Invoice uses ISSUED_TO, not FOR_COMPANY.
(Company)-[:OWNED_BY]->(User) for the account owner.
cypher_template: MATCH (co:Company) RETURN co.industry AS industry, count(co) AS accounts ORDER BY accounts DESC
examples: How many accounts do we have?
Which contacts work at this account?
search_text: account Company CompanySite WORKS_AT WITH_COMPANY ISSUED_TO HAS_SITE parent company client

name: Revenue / Order Volume
description: Order value and count. Two separate stores: CDP Order (self-serve / commerce) and CRM SalesOrder (sales-led).
disambiguation: Order and SalesOrder are distinct nodes with distinct keys and distinct amount fields. Order.order_id / Order.total_amount versus SalesOrder.id / SalesOrder.total. Answer from ONE of them and name which, or return them as two labelled rows. Never add them together silently. Invoice.total is billed revenue, a third thing again — use it only for billing questions.
business_rules: CDP: (Contact)-[:PLACED]->(Order), amount field total_amount, date field created_at.
CRM: (SalesOrder)-[:PLACED_BY]->(Contact) and (SalesOrder)-[:FOR_COMPANY]->(Company), amount field total, date field confirmed_at (created_at for booked-but-unconfirmed).
Line detail: (SalesOrder)-[:HAS_LINE]->(OrderLine)-[:FOR_PRODUCT]->(Product) for CRM; (Order)-[:CONTAINS]->(Product) for CDP. HAS_LINE is also used by Quote and Invoice — label both ends.
Group by currency or filter to a single currency. Both nodes carry a currency property.
There is no (Tenant)-[:HAS_SALES_ORDER]->() edge.
cypher_template: MATCH (o:Order) WHERE o.created_at >= datetime($period_start) AND o.created_at < datetime($period_end) RETURN o.currency AS currency, count(o) AS order_count, sum(toFloat(o.total_amount)) AS revenue ORDER BY revenue DESC
alternate_template: MATCH (so:SalesOrder) WHERE so.confirmed_at >= datetime($period_start) AND so.confirmed_at < datetime($period_end) RETURN so.currency AS currency, count(so) AS order_count, sum(toFloat(so.total)) AS revenue ORDER BY revenue DESC
search_text: revenue order volume total_amount SalesOrder total PLACED PLACED_BY currency GMV bookings

name: Billing and Invoicing
description: Invoices issued to companies, and the contracts they recur under. There is no BillingCycle node — the cycle is inferred from Contract dates and Invoice issue dates.
business_rules: Invoice.issue_date is a DATE. Compare with date($period_start), NOT datetime($period_start) — mixing the two raises a Neo4j type error and the agent returns nothing.
due_at and paid_at ARE datetimes. Overdue = paid_at IS NULL AND due_at < datetime().
(Invoice)-[:ISSUED_TO]->(Company), (Invoice)-[:FOR_ORDER]->(SalesOrder), (Invoice)-[:FOR_DEAL]->(Deal), (Invoice)-[:HAS_LINE]->(InvoiceLine).
(Contract)-[:FOR_COMPANY]->(Company), (Contract)-[:FROM_DEAL]->(Deal), (Contract)-[:RENEWED_BY]->(Deal). Contract.arr is the recurring value; starts_at / ends_at bound the term.
Invoice carries total, tax_amount and discount_amount separately — 'billed' normally means total. Say which you used.
There is no (Tenant)-[:HAS_INVOICE]->() or (Tenant)-[:HAS_CONTRACT]->() edge.
cypher_template: MATCH (inv:Invoice)-[:ISSUED_TO]->(co:Company) WHERE inv.issue_date >= date($period_start) AND inv.issue_date < date($period_end) RETURN co.name AS company, inv.currency AS currency, count(inv) AS invoices, sum(toFloat(inv.total)) AS billed ORDER BY billed DESC LIMIT 10
alternate_template: MATCH (inv:Invoice)-[:ISSUED_TO]->(co:Company) WHERE inv.paid_at IS NULL AND inv.due_at < datetime() RETURN co.name AS company, count(inv) AS overdue_invoices, sum(toFloat(inv.total)) AS overdue_amount ORDER BY overdue_amount DESC LIMIT 10
examples: What did we bill this month?
search_text: billing invoice issue_date due_at paid_at ISSUED_TO Contract arr renewal overdue outstanding

name: Product Catalog
description: Sellable inventory products, plus the CRM commercial overlays: offers, addons, tiers and price books.
disambiguation: There are TWO product notions. Product (inventory.products, key id, a real sellable item with sku, price, stock_on_hand) and PlatformProduct (a stub label with a STRING id, used only to say which Worktual module a Role, VoiceDid or KnowledgeDocument belongs to). A question about what the tenant sells means Product. A question about module access means PlatformProduct. Matching the wrong one returns bare stub nodes with no name property, which is a common source of empty or nonsense answers.
business_rules: (Tenant)-[:OFFERS]->(Product) DOES exist and is safe.
(ProductOffer)-[:FOR_PRODUCT]->(Product), (Addon)-[:FOR_PRODUCT]->(Product), (Addon)-[:HAS_TIER]->(AddonTier).
(PriceBook)-[:LISTS]->(PriceBookEntry), then (PriceBookEntry)-[:FOR_PRODUCT|FOR_OFFER|FOR_ADDON]->(...). The entry is the child of the price book — the edge is LISTS, direction PriceBook to entry.

FOR_PRODUCT is heavily overloaded — it also runs from Role, VoiceDid, KnowledgeDocument and PriceBookEntry to PlatformProduct. Always label both ends or you will pull module stubs into a catalog answer.
PlatformProduct nodes have only an id. They have no name, no price and no properties to report.
Sales quantities come from QuoteLine, OrderLine and InvoiceLine, all reached with HAS_LINE from their parent and FOR_PRODUCT to Product.
cypher_template: MATCH (p:Product) WHERE p.status = $status RETURN p.category AS category, count(p) AS products, avg(toFloat(p.price)) AS avg_price ORDER BY products DESC
alternate_template: MATCH (so:SalesOrder)-[:HAS_LINE]->(ol:OrderLine)-[:FOR_PRODUCT]->(p:Product) WHERE so.confirmed_at >= datetime($period_start) AND so.confirmed_at < datetime($period_end) RETURN p.name AS product, sum(toFloat(ol.quantity)) AS units, sum(toFloat(ol.amount)) AS revenue ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 10
examples: What is in the default price book?
search_text: product catalog SKU price book offer addon tier FOR_PRODUCT OFFERS LISTS PlatformProduct stub

name: Period-over-Period Comparison
description: How to answer any 'did X go up or down' question in a single query.
business_rules: Bind all four params: $period_start, $period_end, $compare_start, $compare_end. Never leave $period_end unbound.
One query with conditional aggregation, not two count queries — two queries can straddle a CDC write and disagree.
Always return current, previous, delta and pct_change. pct_change must be guarded: CASE WHEN previous = 0 THEN null ELSE round(100.0*(current-previous)/previous, 1) END.
If previous = 0 and current > 0, do not report an infinite increase — say the comparison window has no prior data.

Check that the comparison window is actually covered by the data before asserting a trend: MATCH (n:Label) RETURN min(n.created_at) AS earliest. A metric that 'tripled' because CDC backfill started mid-window is a wrong answer, not an insight.
This card has NO executable cypher of its own. Take the cypher_template or diagnostic_template from the metric card and wrap it in the CASE WHEN pattern. Do not emit this card's text as a query.
pattern_template: MATCH (<node pattern from the metric card>) WITH <dimension expression> AS dimension, sum(CASE WHEN <date_field> >= datetime($period_start) AND <date_field> < datetime($period_end) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS current, sum(CASE WHEN <date_field> >= datetime($compare_start) AND <date_field> < datetime($compare_end) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS previous WHERE current > 0 OR previous > 0 RETURN dimension, current, previous, current - previous AS delta, CASE WHEN previous = 0 THEN null ELSE round(100.0*(current-previous)/previous, 1) END AS pct_change ORDER BY abs(current - previous) DESC LIMIT 5
examples: Why did X increase this week?
Compare this month vs last month
search_text: period over period comparison week over week month over month delta pct change increase decrease trend

name: Top Contributors Breakdown
description: How to rank dimensions by their contribution to a change.
business_rules: Rank by abs(delta), not by current volume — the biggest queue is usually not the one that changed.
Limit to 5 dimensions and stop after naming the top 3 in the answer.
Filter out dimensions where current = 0 AND previous = 0, otherwise the result is padded with dead queues.

Available dimensions by metric: contact-centre metrics split by Queue.name, Conversation.channel, Agent.display_name, MissedContact.reason, RoutingAttempt.outcome, SLA.name. CRM metrics split by Deal.stage, ContactProfile.lead_source, Company.industry, User (owner).
This card has no executable cypher. It selects a dimension for the metric card's diagnostic_template.
search_text: top contributors breakdown dimension delta root cause drivers ranking
